approach: Root cause: tests wrote executable stand-ins in-process (open, write, chmod, then exec), which fails with ETXTBSY when another thread forks while the write handle is open. There was no single helper and no mechanical list of write sites, so each job patched one site. The base tree already has a helper (`athena_git::script_writer::write_executable`, an `sh` child doing `cat > tmp && chmod 755 tmp && mv tmp final`), a public module of a production crate, and most sites already use it. What remains is the part that lets the class return. (1) Create the std-only crate `athena-testkit` and move the helper there, to be the one place that writes a stand-in; delete `athena_git::script_writer`. (2) Convert the last in-process site, `crates/athena-cli/tests/slot_exec.rs:53-54`. (3) Re-point the existing callers to `athena_testkit::write_executable` through dev-dependencies. (4) Remove the busy-retry in `reading.rs` `check_stub`. (5) Add `tests/no_in_process_exec_writes.rs`, a `syn` scan of every `.rs` file in the workspace. It fails on any executable write in test code outside the helper: `set_permissions`, `from_mode`, `set_mode`, one-argument `.mode(..)`, `Command::new("chmod")`, and calls to production wrapper functions found by name. Planted-violation unit tests prove each detector. (6) Add `tests/stand_in_stress.rs`. (7) Update docs, decision log, links, shard timings and CHANGELOG. No production behaviour changes.

decisions.choice: One helper in a new std-only crate `athena-testkit`, used as a dev-dependency only, replacing `athena_git::script_writer`.
decisions.reason: Criterion 1 names `athena_testkit::write_executable`. A crate with no Athena dependencies can be a dev-dependency of every crate without touching the documented normal-dependency graph (`graph_problems` in xtask/tests/policy.rs:415 reads only `kind` null edges). It also removes a test helper from the public API of a production crate (athena-git).

rejected.option: Keep `athena_git::script_writer` and add a second helper in testkit
rejected.why: Two helpers is the original problem again, and a scan would need an exemption for each.
Gives a production crate a normal dependency on a test crate and breaks the documented rule that athena-git is a leaf.

rejected.option: Retry on ETXTBSY at run sites (existing `check_stub`, `retry_busy`)
rejected.why: Patches symptoms site by site; out of scope and the brief asks to remove the test retry.

decisions.choice: Detect with a `syn` scan over all `.rs` files of crates/*/src, crates/*/tests, xtask/src and xtask/tests. Test code means: files under `tests/`, `test_support.rs`, `testutil.rs`, files named by a `#[cfg(test)] mod x;` declaration (matched by stem), and items under `#[cfg(..test..)]` (not under `not(..)`) or `#[test]`. Macro token streams in test code are walked too.
decisions.reason: Real parsing sees calls inside nested modules, closures and `cfg` attributes, and walking macro tokens closes the `assert!(..)` gap. It adopts `syn`, already a workspace dependency (buy-first).

rejected.why: Misses wrappers such as `set_executable(&fake)`, and flags strings and comments.
Most stand-in sites are `#[cfg(test)]` modules inside src files.

decisions.choice: Wrapper resolution is one level and by name. Collect names of non-test `fn`s anywhere in the workspace whose body (macro tokens included) calls `set_permissions`, `from_mode`, `set_mode` or `Command::new("chmod")`. Flag test-code calls to those names. Names of test-code fns are not collected. A reviewed allow-list `(path, enclosing fn, reason)` holds known false positives. A test asserts each entry still matches a real hit, so entries cannot go stale.
decisions.reason: This makes `set_executable(&fake)` (the xtask wrapper) a hit. Test-code wrappers are flagged at their own definition. A generic test helper name like `script` (250 uses in `script(` form across 23 files, by Grep count) would otherwise cause false positives. A transitive closure would flag every test that calls production code which eventually chmods.

rejected.why: Flags tests that merely call production code that sets modes (for example snapshot materialisation); the signal is lost.
`crates/athena-cli/src/slot_exec.rs` fn `script` (line 126) writes a file with a variable mode that `find_program` only reads; it is never executed, and that file is not a deliverable.

decisions.choice: Stress test: assert the helper variant records 0 ETXTBSY over 4 writer threads x 100 cycles with 4 forking threads. The in-process variant's count is written with `std::io::stderr().write_all` (libtest captures only print macros) and is not asserted, because it is a race. A separate deterministic test holds a write handle open and shows exec fails with ETXTBSY.
decisions.reason: Makes the count visible in the recorded output without `--nocapture`, without a flaky `> 0` assertion, and shows that the failure the helper prevents is real.

rejected.option: Assert the in-process hit count is above 0
rejected.why: Nondeterministic; would make the suite flaky, the very failure class being fixed.
Captured on pass, so invisible without `--nocapture`.

decisions.reason: It has no permission or executable writes (Grep for set_permissions/from_mode/#!/bin found none), so there is nothing to convert. It is only treated as test code by the scan.

rejected.option: Touch it to match the deliverable list

risks.risk: The scan reports false positives on generic names or on production wrappers called from tests.
risks.mitigation: Treat a name as a wrapper only if it is a non-test fn that calls a base primitive, never collect test fns, resolve one level only, and keep a reviewed allow-list with a staleness test. The producer reads every tree hit before allow-listing one.

risks.risk: The scan misses a form of in-process executable write (a false sense of completeness).
risks.mitigation: Document the exact covered forms in the test file's header. Walk macro tokens in test code. The planted tests cover each form. Known gaps are named: copying an executable (`fs::copy`), unpacking archives (`tar::unpack`) and shell strings passed to `sh -c`.

risks.risk: The stress test is itself flaky or slow.
risks.mitigation: Do not assert on the in-process count; assert only the helper's 0. The deterministic held-handle test does not depend on timing.

risks.risk: The in-process variant leaves many temp files or slows CI.
risks.mitigation: The stress test uses 4x100 cycles like the existing script_writer test, which ran in the suite; the producer measures runtime and trims cycles if the file exceeds the 10 s estimate in shard-timings.
Run `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` once without `--locked` so cargo writes the lock offline (all crates are already locked), then run the checks with `--locked`.
